Pod: The smallest thing Kubernetes runs: one or more containers that share a network address and storage.
label: A key and value tag on an object, such as app: web. Other objects use labels to find it.
image: A packaged app with everything it needs to run. Kubernetes downloads it from a registry.
port: A numbered door on a network address. A web server usually listens on port 80.
Deployment: An object that keeps a set number of identical Pods running and rolls out changes to them.
replica: One copy of a Pod. Several replicas share the work and keep the app up if one fails.
selector: A rule that picks objects by their labels, such as every Pod labelled app: web.
Pod template: The part of a Deployment that describes each Pod it creates.
ReplicaSet: An object that keeps a set number of identical Pods running. Deployments manage ReplicaSets for you.
request: The CPU or memory a container needs. Kubernetes uses it to choose a node with enough room.
limit: The most CPU or memory a container may use.
namespace: A named group inside a cluster. Names only need to be unique within one namespace.
ConfigMap: An object that stores settings as text, so you can change them without rebuilding the image.
environment variable: A named value a program reads when it starts, such as DB_USER=app-user.
volume: Storage that containers in a Pod can mount as a folder.
Secret: An object for small private values, such as passwords. Stored base64-encoded, which is not encryption.
Job: An object that runs Pods until a task finishes successfully.
CronJob: An object that creates a Job on a repeating schedule, written in cron format.
